theme: 3 terms on what a String is made of: its bytes, its code numbers, and the characters people actually see

terms.definition: A view of a String as the raw bytes it uses in UTF-8 encoding.
terms.example: The API limit is in bytes, so check the UTF-8 View, not `count`.

terms.definition: A single Unicode code, a number that stands for one symbol or one part of a symbol.
terms.example: The accent is a separate Unicode Scalar, so the search missed it.

terms.definition: One or more Unicode Scalars that show up together as a single character on screen.
terms.example: A flag is one Grapheme Cluster, even though it's two scalars.
terms.code:
let flag = "\u{1F1F0}\u{1F1F7}"  // Korea
print(flag.count)
print(flag.unicodeScalars.count)
print(flag.utf8.count)

quizzes.question: In this code, `flag.count` is 1 because its two codes form one what?
What do you call a single code number that stands for one symbol or part of one?
What gives you a String's raw bytes, for example to check a byte limit?

video.title: UTF-8 View, Unicode Scalar & Grapheme Cluster | Day 49
video.description:
Learn to explain what a Swift String is made of: UTF-8 View, Unicode Scalar & Grapheme Cluster, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
UTF-8 View - A view of a String as the raw bytes it uses in UTF-8 encoding.
Unicode Scalar - A single Unicode code, a number that stands for one symbol or one part of a symbol.
Grapheme Cluster - One or more Unicode Scalars that show up together as a single character on screen.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift UTF-8 View, Unicode Scalar & Grapheme Cluster | Day 49
landscape.description:
Explain UTF-8 View, Unicode Scalar & Grapheme Cluster in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
UTF-8 뷰, 유니코드 스칼라, 그래핌 클러스터 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

UTF-8 View - A view of a String as the raw bytes it uses in UTF-8 encoding.
한국어: UTF-8 뷰: String을 UTF-8 인코딩의 원시 바이트로 보는 뷰

Unicode Scalar - A single Unicode code, a number that stands for one symbol or one part of a symbol.
한국어: 유니코드 스칼라: 기호 하나 또는 기호의 일부를 나타내는 유니코드 코드 번호 하나

Grapheme Cluster - One or more Unicode Scalars that show up together as a single character on screen.
한국어: 그래핌 클러스터: 화면에서 한 글자로 함께 보이는 하나 이상의 유니코드 스칼라

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why a four-letter name is six bytes, what an accent really is and what count counts, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Unicode in Swift in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `name` is José, four letters. Why does the server say six?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The server counts bytes. That's the UTF-8 View, not the letters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the accent takes extra bytes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Here the accent is its own Unicode Scalar, and it needs two bytes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Its own Unicode Scalar? I only see one letter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The e and the accent form one Grapheme Cluster.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So for the server limit, I check the UTF-8 View?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Check `utf8.count` for the server, and `count` for what users see.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Grapheme Cluster for letters, Unicode Scalar for codes, UTF-8 View for bytes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The limit is 100 bytes, not letters.
